codebaseContext: Calculo Gratis - Brazilian calculator platform (Next.js SSG)

vulnerabilities.title: Plaintext Storage of Sensitive Data
vulnerabilities.description: Memory and session data stored in JSON files without encryption. If secrets are persisted here, they would be readable in plaintext. File permissions not explicitly restricted.
vulnerabilities.evidence: fs.writeFileSync(MEMORY_FILE, JSON.stringify(memory, null, 2)); - no mode specified
vulnerabilities.impact: Any secrets stored via memory.set() would be vulnerable to disclosure if file permissions allow other users to read .claude-flow/data/
vulnerabilities.recommendation: 1) Never store secrets in memory.js. 2) Set restrictive file permissions (0600) when writing: fs.writeFileSync(file, data, {mode: 0o600}). 3) Consider using encrypted storage library for sensitive data.

vulnerabilities.title: Session Files Created Without Restricted Permissions
vulnerabilities.description: Session files are created without specifying file mode, defaulting to system umask. This could allow other users on the system to read session context data.
vulnerabilities.impact: On shared systems, other users might read session state including context variables that could contain tokens or credentials.
vulnerabilities.recommendation: Set file mode to 0o600 when writing session files: fs.writeFileSync(file, data, {mode: 0o600})

vulnerabilities.title: No Validation on Stored Values
vulnerabilities.description: The set() function validates key format but not value content. Malicious or excessively large values could be stored.
vulnerabilities.evidence: memory[key] = value; // value parameter has no size or format checks
vulnerabilities.impact: Potential for DoS via large values or unvalidated data storage.
vulnerabilities.recommendation: Add validation: const MAX_VALUE_SIZE = 1000000; if (value && value.length > MAX_VALUE_SIZE) throw new Error('Value too large')

vulnerabilities.title: Attempts to Read Potentially Sensitive Paths
vulnerabilities.description: The statusline.js attempts to read from hardcoded paths like .swarm/security and .claude/security-scans without proper validation.
vulnerabilities.impact: Could leak information about system configuration or security scan results if accessible.
vulnerabilities.recommendation: 1) Validate paths exist and are readable. 2) Consider if reading security scan results should be restricted. 3) Use path.resolve() and check for directory traversal risks.

vulnerabilities.title: Temporary File Cleanup Could Fail Silently
vulnerabilities.description: Temporary files are cleaned up in finally block with try-catch that ignores errors. If cleanup fails repeatedly, orphaned temp files could accumulate.
vulnerabilities.evidence: try { unlinkSync(tmpFile); } catch (e) { // Ignore cleanup errors }
vulnerabilities.impact: Disk space exhaustion from accumulated temp files (low probability).
vulnerabilities.recommendation: Log cleanup failures for monitoring: if (cleanup failed) console.warn('Failed to clean up', tmpFile)

vulnerabilities.title: Analytics and AdSense Client IDs in Build Output
vulnerabilities.description: NEXT_PUBLIC_GA_MEASUREMENT_ID and NEXT_PUBLIC_ADSENSE_CLIENT are exposed in client-side code. While these are intended to be public, verify they don't contain sensitive identifiers.
vulnerabilities.evidence: window.dataLayer.push with gtag configuration; adsbygoogle setup with client ID
vulnerabilities.impact: These IDs could be used for tracking or account enumeration if they follow predictable patterns.
vulnerabilities.recommendation: 1) Verify these are actual GA and AdSense IDs (safe to expose). 2) Monitor for unusual usage patterns. 3) Rotate if compromised.

vulnerabilities.title: No Input Validation for CLI Execution
vulnerabilities.description: Router CLI doesn't validate task input or handle edge cases before processing.
vulnerabilities.evidence: const task = process.argv.slice(2).join(' '); - no validation before routing
vulnerabilities.impact: Could be exploited with malicious task descriptions.
vulnerabilities.recommendation: Add input validation: const MAX_TASK_LENGTH = 500; if (!task || task.length > MAX_TASK_LENGTH) process.exit(1)

✓ github-safe.js uses spawnSync preventing shell injection attacks
✓ All external command execution properly escaped

✓ Next.js framework provides automatic XSS protection via React escaping
✓ No SQL injection vectors detected (no database queries in analyzable code)

recommendations.action: Set restrictive file permissions on helper script file writes
recommendations.details: Update memory.js and session.js to use fs.writeFileSync(file, data, {mode: 0o600}) to prevent other system users from reading sensitive files.

recommendations.action: Implement input validation in CLI helpers
recommendations.details: Add size and format validation to memory.js, session.js, and router.js to prevent DoS and injection attacks.
Log failures in temp file cleanup and file permission issues for better monitoring.
Add security section to CLAUDE.md about what should/shouldn't be stored in memory and session files.
Confirm GA_MEASUREMENT_ID and ADSENSE_CLIENT are legitimate public identifiers, not sensitive tokens.
Execute 'npm audit' to check dependencies for known vulnerabilities. Add to CI/CD pipeline.
